title: Name the steps, never number them
statement: Name each procedure step in its own words, on screen and aloud, never by a number, which only signals unseen steps, and say the procedure's name whenever it runs.
detail: The course renderer's pedagogy rules require a modelling moment to say which of its seven procedures it is running and to show the step it is on, named and never numbered, on screen or aloud (`othello-course-renderer-draft/repo/docs/rules/pedagogy-and-lesson-structure.md`, lines 327-345). A label such as "Step two, part a" tells a child only that unseen steps are coming, while the step's own words are the teaching. The procedure specification behind the rule treats steps as student-facing, to be displayed, spoken and internalised (`othello-course-renderer-draft/repo/docs/pedagogy/modelling-moment-procedures.md`, line 24). The same rules also have the procedure's name said each time it runs, since a child who watched one procedure four times without once hearing its name had four demonstrations and no tool.
against: The same repository's QA invariants require step numbers that are sequential and unique per beat, with never two "Step 2" blocks (`othello-course-renderer-draft/repo/docs/qa/new-lesson-qa-invariants.md`, lines 34-35), and the procedure specification voices the search with the step numbers, as in "Step 1, Read the question…" (`othello-course-renderer-draft/repo/docs/pedagogy/modelling-moment-procedures.md`, lines 838 and 840). The course's QA invariants check numbers: "**A3. Step numbering is sequential and unique per beat.** Never two "Step 2" blocks; never a Step 3 numbered 2." (`grade3-reading/course-renderer/docs/qa/new-lesson-qa-invariants.md`, lines 34-35), and a built lesson decided on "One ladder everywhere, matching the p17 chart and the p25 recap: Step 1 Read the question, Step 2 Find it in the text, Step 3 State the answer, Step 4 Refine the concept, Step 5 Let's try extra thinking." (`grade3-reading/course-renderer/content/lesson-plans/g3-u2-l1.json`, line 760).

evidence.quote: The step is named, never numbered, on screen or aloud.
"Step two, part a" tells a child only that steps they have not seen are coming and that they cannot see how many
Seven named procedures are the whole design: a child who has watched FIND four times without once hearing it called FIND has been given four demonstrations and no tool.
**Rule.** A modelling moment says which of the seven procedures it is running and shows the step the guide is on, advancing as the voice reaches it.
Steps are student-facing. They can be displayed on screen, spoken aloud, and internalised.
**A3. Step numbering is sequential and unique per beat.** Never two "Step 2" blocks; never a Step 3 numbered 2.
voiced once inside the think-aloud with the step numbers
The step is named, never numbered, on screen or aloud.

"Step two, part a" tells a child only that steps they have not seen are coming and that they cannot see how many; the step's own words, "What is the main thing in each part?", are the whole of the teaching.
